clue.text: Gulf City, Japanese mount, securing Ascot’s first cheer

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece is gripped inside another

blocks.note: rah is a shout of encouragement

explanation.surface: A travel note pairing a Gulf city with Mount Fuji and a cheer at Ascot races.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter goes between the last two letters of the mountain. Ascot is the English racecourse, and 'Gulf' is the Persian Gulf region.
explanation.definitionFit: Fujairah is one of the seven emirates of the UAE and its capital, on the Gulf of Oman coast.

clue.text: Read cons will be waiving right

indicators.note: to waive something is to give it up, so these letters are dropped

blocks.note: to construe a text is to read or interpret it

explanation.surface: Someone reading about prisoners, or swindles, who are giving up a right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cons' looks like convicts, but it is just the four letters to strip from the front of CONSTRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: True and right both describe something correct or accurate, as in 'the right answer'.

clue.text: Wine-carrier fine muddling along

indicators.note: muddling things mixes them up, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A wine-bearer stumbling along nicely, perhaps having sampled the goods.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the flagon of the 'flagon with the dragon' line from the Danny Kaye film The Court Jester.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large vessel with a handle and spout for holding and serving wine.

clue.text: The authority with which one rules one’s robes a joke

definitions.text: The authority with which one rules

indicators.note: to robe is to clothe, so one piece is wrapped around another

blocks.note: a speaker's own possessive: one's, from my point of view

explanation.surface: A monarch whose ceremonial robes are so outlandish they have become a laughing stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as the speaker's own, MY, and its two letters are split around A JEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Majesty is the sovereign power and dignity of a monarch, the authority by which a king or queen reigns.

clue.text: It’s payback time for us English, landing in States

definitions.note: the definition is the 'us' who speak the phrase

indicators.note: something landing in a place ends up inside it

blocks.note: to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: English visitors arriving in the United States declare it is time for revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' looks like the USA, but it is the verb: avers.
explanation.definitionFit: People seeking revenge or retribution would declare that the moment for getting even has come.

clue.text: A rising couturier Nick dresses like a star

indicators.note: in a down clue rising reads upwards, so the letters run backwards
to dress something is to clothe it, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: to nick is to steal, in British slang
Christian Dior, the French fashion designer

explanation.surface: Up-and-coming designer Nick clothes his clients so they look like celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like the designer's first name but is British slang for pilfering, and 'dresses' is the verb, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Asteroidal means star-shaped or resembling a star, from Greek aster.

clue.text: Employee of 14 bar counsel at first oddly rejects

indicators.note: bar as a preposition means except, so a letter is excluded
at first points to the opening letter alone
oddly suggests something out of its normal order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A legal worker at court whose advice is strangely rejected by the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' and 'counsel' suggest barristers, but bar means except. 14 is THE COURT, so the employee is the court jester, the theme of the Danny Kaye film.
explanation.definitionFit: A jester was a professional fool kept in a royal household to entertain the monarch and courtiers.

clue.text: This fighter set out to damage legislature

indicators.note: out means removed, so these letters are taken away
damaging something breaks its shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An insurgent who set out to wreck the parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' reads as a phrasal verb meaning began, but SET is the fodder to remove and 'out' is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerilla is an irregular fighter in a small independent band, often attacking the established government.

clue.text: Split personalities then repair boat?

definitions.note: a boat is one example of a vessel, hence the question mark

indicators.note: splitting cuts a word in two, so its halves can be rejoined the other way round

explanation.surface: A patient with split personalities is told to go and fix a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repair' is re-pair: the two halves of the split word are paired again the other way. VESSEL is in the 'vessel with the pestle' line of The Court Jester.
explanation.definitionFit: Vessel is the general word for any ship or craft, so a boat is one example of it.

clue.text: Right to back vote for a woman

indicators.note: the right-hand end of a word is its last letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: aye is a vote in favour

explanation.surface: Someone claiming the right to support a vote for a female candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a verb meaning support, but it is the word whose right-hand letter is taken. Danny Kaye starred in The Court Jester, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaye is a female given name, as well as a surname, so a woman could be called it.

clue.text: More than one competent fighter strips outside town

blocks.note: first meaning: martial artists of middle rank, competent but not yet experts
second meaning: protected bands of countryside around cities

explanation.walkthrough: 'strips' could be a verb, as if fighters undress outside town, but it is a noun. A green belt in Britain is undeveloped land ringing a city where building is restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: In judo and karate the coloured belt marks grade, and in planning the term names protected rural land encircling urban areas.

clue.text: Entity issuing fire, like working TV?

blocks.note: a TV, short for transvestite, wears women's clothing, or drag
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A television that bursts into flames once it is switched on.
explanation.walkthrough: TV looks like television, but it is the abbreviation for transvestite, someone in drag. DRAGON is in the 'flagon with the dragon' line of The Court Jester.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragon is the mythical winged reptile famous for breathing out flames.

clue.text: Good Catholic is still looking after aging birds

indicators.note: to look after something is to hold it in one's care, so one piece takes in another

explanation.surface: A devout Catholic who still cares for his elderly birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good Catholic' reads as one devout person, but it is two abbreviations; the aging piece is tucked in just after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldcrests are tiny European songbirds with a yellow crown stripe, the smallest birds in Britain.

clue.text: Italian writer admitted time was not kind to those hearing this case

indicators.note: something admitted is let inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: to hurt someone is to treat them unkindly
Umberto Eco, author of The Name of the Rose

explanation.surface: An Italian author confesses in court that time has been cruel to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' sounds like a confession in the dock, but it tells you T plus HURT lets ECO in.
explanation.definitionFit: A court is the judge and jury, or the tribunal, who listen to the evidence in a legal case.

clue.text: Sort of mechanical man’s knocked out of cup

indicators.note: something knocked out of a thing is removed from it
to sort something is to arrange it, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A robot has been knocked out of the cup competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of mechanical' reads as 'somewhat mechanical'; the letters of MAN go first, then the rest are rearranged. CHALICE opens the 'chalice from the palace' line of The Court Jester.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalice is a large goblet or drinking cup, especially one used at communion.

clue.text: After correspondence, friend departs to the far south

indicators.note: in a down entry the far south is the bottom, so a letter is moved to the very end

blocks.note: a compadre is a friend or companion; its D is the letter that travels
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: Having received letters, a friend leaves for the far south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correspondence' suggests letters, but here it means likeness: things are compared after one checks how they correspond.
explanation.definitionFit: Two items that have been compared have been set side by side to judge how closely they match each other.

clue.text: Writer emphatically does not like the teeth of some animals

definitions.text: like the teeth of some animals

blocks.note: the writer of the clue refers to himself in the first person
so used as an intensifier, as in 'I so want that'
contraction of do not, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: An author declares his strong distaste for animal teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like' looks like the verb to be fond of, but it belongs to the definition, meaning similar to.
explanation.definitionFit: Isodont describes teeth that are all of the same size and shape, as in many reptiles.

clue.text: Refinement links to the French Riviera?

definitions.note: singular definition for a plural answer

blocks.note: Nice is the main city of the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A touch of class: having connections to the Côte d'Azur.
explanation.walkthrough: The French Riviera stands for its best-known city.
explanation.definitionFit: Niceties are fine points of etiquette or detail, the small elegances that mark refinement.

clue.text: Broadcast grenade warning on the piste

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A radio alert that a grenade is lying on the ski slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piste' suggests skiing, but a piste is also the strip on which fencers fight.
explanation.definitionFit: En garde is the call a fencer gives to the opponent to take the ready position before a bout.

clue.text: Armstrong, say – or GNORTSMRA?

blocks.note: the astronaut's surname written in capitals and turned round: a name in caps

explanation.surface: A quiz asking whether the moonwalker is Armstrong, or his name printed backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: GNORTSMRA is a NAME in CAPS, run backwards; so run NAME CAPS backwards too. Neil Armstrong was the first man on the Moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Armstrong is the most famous example of an astronaut, a traveller beyond Earth's atmosphere.

clue.text: Rising marksman recording shot

indicators.note: in a down entry rising reads from the bottom up, so the letters go backwards

blocks.note: William Tell, the archer who shot an apple off his son's head
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming sharpshooter has a video of the shot.
explanation.walkthrough: The PELLET is from the 'pellet with the poison' line of The Court Jester.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot is the collective term for the small lead balls fired from a shotgun, each one a pellet.

clue.text: It houses royal secretary who’s paid to assist doctor …

blocks.note: a PA, personal assistant, is a secretary paid to help
to doctor a drink is to lace it

explanation.surface: A royal secretary is employed to help the court physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a physician but is the verb, to spike or tamper with. This is the palace of 'the chalice from the palace'.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is the official residence where a monarch or royal family lives.

clue.text: Corrupt chamber appears to be working

blocks.note: a po is a chamber pot
something that appears operational is on

explanation.surface: A corrupt legislative chamber still seems to be functioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chamber' suggests a parliament, but it is the chamber pot, PO. The poison is in 'the pellet with the poison'.
explanation.definitionFit: To poison something is to taint or corrupt it, morally as well as physically.

clue.text: … the King was in this depressed state

explanation.surface: Continuing the royal tale: the king was in a gloomy condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the King' sounds like a royal, but it is Elvis Presley, and 'state' is a US state, not a mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue Hawaii is the 1961 musical film in which Elvis Presley, nicknamed the King, played the lead.

clue.text: A selection of Turkish tobacco rolling one way and the other

indicators.note: a selection is a run picked from a larger whole, so the letters lie inside the words
something rolling turns over, so the letters come out backwards

explanation.surface: Someone rolling cigarettes from mixed Turkish tobacco, first one way then the other.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the last letter of Turkish and takes the first three of tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: Both covers each of two alternatives together, so it fits 'this way and that' taken jointly.

clue.text: Beer in a fancy wine bar’s neglected

indicators.note: something neglected is left out, so these letters are dropped
fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: In an upmarket wine bar the beer goes ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' reads as part of the setting, but those three letters are struck from WINE BAR before the rest is rearranged. BREW is in 'the brew that is true'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brew is an informal word for beer, from the brewing that produces it.

clue.text: Quietly great player acquires instrument for a pound?

indicators.note: to acquire something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: st is a hushing sound asking for quiet

explanation.surface: A star footballer quietly buys an instrument for just one pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quietly' looks like P, the musical piano, but it is ST, the hush sound. 'a pound' means an act of pounding, not money. The pestle is in 'the vessel with the pestle'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pestle is the club-shaped tool used to crush and grind things in a mortar.

clue.text: Is it Lynam and O’Connor circling one officer sees?

indicators.note: to circle something is to go round it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: Des Lynam and Des O'Connor, two British TV presenters both called Des

explanation.surface: A question whether two veteran TV hosts are surrounding an officer who is watching.
explanation.walkthrough: The two presenters share a first name, so together they are that name made plural. 'sees' is not the verb but the plural of see, a bishop's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's area of authority, and diocese is the more common word for that territory.
